text: Launch 1-Click Clusters of 16 to 512 NVIDIA H100 or B200 GPUs with GPUDirect RDMA interconnect at up to 3200 Gb/s
quote: 1-Click Clusters (1CC) are high-performance clusters composed of both GPU and CPU nodes, featuring 16 to 512 NVIDIA H100 or B200 SXM Tensor Core GPUs...enabling peer-to-peer GPUDirect RDMA at up to 3200 Gb/s

text: Spin up GPU clusters instantly or start with a single-node instance
quote: Launch 16x to 512x NVIDIA H100 or B200 GPU clusters instantly, or start with a single-node instance.

text: No long-term commitments required
quote: No long-term commitments.

text: Production-ready clusters scale from 16 to more than 2,000 B200 or H100 GPUs
quote: Production-ready clusters from 16 to 2,000+ NVIDIA B200 or H100 GPUs.

text: Reserve a 1-Click Cluster self-serve from the cloud console
quote: Navigate to the 1-Click Clusters page in the Lambda Cloud console and click Reserve 1-Click Cluster.

text: Quick start goes from SSH to a first multi-node GPU job in minutes
quote: The quick start takes you from SSH to your first multi-node GPU job in minutes.

text: Each 1-Click Cluster includes three CPU head nodes for bastion access, administration and job scheduling
quote: Each 1CC includes 3x CPU management (head) nodes for use as jump boxes (bastion hosts) and for cluster administration and job scheduling.

text: On-Demand Cloud gives on-demand access to Linux GPU-backed virtual machine instances
quote: On-Demand Cloud (ODC) provides on-demand access to Linux-based, GPU-backed virtual machine instances.

text: Self-serve deployment of B200, H100, A100 or GH200 instances in minutes
quote: Deploy NVIDIA B200, H100, A100, or GH200 instances in minutes with self-serve, first-come access.

text: Predefined instance types include HGX B200, GH200 Grace Hopper and H100 GPUs
quote: ODC offers a variety of predefined instance types to support different workload requirements. Available GPUs include the state-of-the-art NVIDIA HGX B200 GPU, NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip, and NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU

text: Instances run Ubuntu 22.04 with Lambda Stack AI/ML drivers, tools and frameworks preinstalled
quote: By default, each ODC instance runs Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. Lambda also preinstalls Lambda Stack, a standard set of AI/ML-related drivers, tools, and frameworks, on the instance

text: GPU Base image offers a minimal Ubuntu setup with key AI/ML tools and drivers for full Python environment control
quote: GPU Base: An image based on Ubuntu Server that includes a minimal set of key AI/ML tools and drivers. ... Use if: You want a minimal working setup with a high degree of control over your Python environment.

text: Use an alternative base image when launching instances via the API
quote: If you launch your instance using the Lambda Cloud API, you can choose to use an alternative base image instead.

text: Add launch-time configuration with cloud-init when launching via the API
quote: If you're launching your instance with the Lambda Cloud API, you can add launch-time configuration instructions using [cloud-init](https://cloudinit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/).

text: Each instance includes a JupyterLab installation, reachable from the Instances page
quote: each ODC instance provides a JupyterLab installation for creating and managing Jupyter notebooks. You can access your instance's JupyterLab by visiting the Instances page

text: Connect to instances directly over SSH or through the preinstalled JupyterLab server
quote: You can connect to your On-Demand Cloud (ODC) instances directly through SSH or by using the preinstalled JupyterLab server.

text: Import an existing SSH key or generate a new one in the console
quote: You can import an existing key if you have one, or you can generate a new one in the Lambda Cloud console.

text: Cluster nodes are directly accessible, with sudo/root administrator privileges
quote: All nodes are directly accessible, and users have system administrator privileges (sudo or root) across the cluster.

text: REST API endpoints for creating and managing Lambda Cloud resources
quote: The Lambda Cloud API provides a set of REST API endpoints you can use to create\nand manage your Lambda Cloud resources.

text: Launch instances programmatically through the Lambda Cloud API
quote: You can also launch instances programmatically by using the Lambda Cloud API. For details, see Launch instances

text: Restart instances programmatically through the Lambda Cloud API
quote: You can also restart instances programmatically by using the Lambda Cloud API.

text: API endpoints for listing and creating workspaces
quote: List workspacesCreate workspace

text: Webhook notifications to your URL on support ticket events
quote: Lambda can send webhook notifications to your URL when support ticket events occur, enabling near real-time integration with your systems.

text: Attach high-capacity regional filesystems to instances for datasets and system state backup
quote: A _filesystem_ is a high-capacity regional file store you can attach to your instance to store datasets and back up system state.

text: Existing filesystems in the same region can also be attached to an instance
quote: Existing filesystems in the same region can additionally be attached.

text: S3-compatible adapter lets tools like rclone and s5cmd copy and manage filesystem files
quote: This adapter allows you to use S3-compatible tools like `rclone` and `s5cmd` to copy files to and from your filesystems and perform common file operations.

text: Filesystem storage has no minimum storage period and no ingress or egress charges
quote: There is no minimum storage period, and you are not charged for ingress or egress.

text: Instances are priced hourly and billed in one-minute increments
quote: ODC prices instances by hourly usage and bills in one-minute increments.

text: Monthly instance usage can be viewed on the console Usage page
quote: To view your monthly usage, navigate to the [Usage page](https://cloud.lambda.com/usage) in the Lambda Cloud console and then click the **Instances** tab.

text: Clear published pricing for instances, 1-Click Clusters and Superclusters
quote: Clear, straightforward pricing for Instances, 1-Click Clusters™, and Superclusters.

text: Reserved capacity is available at the lowest prices by contacting Lambda
quote: Contact us for reserved capacity at our lowest prices.

text: Firewall rules restrict incoming traffic to workspace instances, including cluster head nodes
quote: You can restrict incoming traffic to the instances in a workspace, including 1-Click Cluster management (head) nodes, by creating firewall rules on the Firewall page

text: Firewall rules can be global to a workspace or scoped to individual instances and regions
quote: You can create global rules that apply to all of the instances in the workspace, or rulesets scoped to individual instances and their regions.

text: Managed Kubernetes on clusters with GPU and InfiniBand RDMA support, shared persistent storage, and no extra setup
quote: MK8s provides a Kubernetes environment with GPU and InfiniBand (RDMA) support, and shared persistent storage across all nodes in a 1CC. Clusters are preconfigured so you can deploy workloads without additional setup.

text: Managed Kubernetes includes automated node remediation for hardware issues
quote: MK8s also includes automated node remediation to detect and recover from hardware issues.

text: Choose Managed Kubernetes, Preinstalled Kubernetes or Slurm as the cluster orchestrator
quote: Choose from Managed Kubernetes, Preinstalled Kubernetes, or Slurm.

text: Managed Slurm is installed, managed and maintained by Lambda, used with standard Slurm tooling
quote: Managed Slurm (MSlurm): Lambda installs, manages, and maintains a Slurm environment on your cluster. You interact with the environment using standard Slurm tooling.

text: Slurm schedules workloads automatically to maximize utilization and prevent resource contention
quote: Slurm automatically schedules workloads, maximizing cluster utilization while preventing resource contention.

text: Lambda monitors and maintains the health of Slurm daemons such as slurmctld and slurmdbd
quote: Lambda monitors and maintains the health of Slurm daemons such as `slurmctld` and `slurmdbd`.

text: Slurm is configured for high availability, so jobs keep running if a head node fails
quote: Slurm is configured for HA, so jobs continue to be schedulable and continue running even if a head node goes down.

text: Lmod loads and unloads cluster software modules such as HPC-X, Node.js and uv
quote: Use Lmod to dynamically load and unload software modules available on the cluster, such as HPC-X, Node.js, and uv.

text: Monitor GPU usage with an NVIDIA DCGM Grafana dashboard
quote: Monitor GPU usage with the NVIDIA DCGM Grafana dashboard.

text: Private Cloud offers single-tenant clusters of 1,000+ GPUs with low-level infrastructure access
quote: Private Cloud is the ideal solution for organizations requiring a single-tenant cluster with 1,000+ GPUs. Private Cloud customers have low-level access to their cluster infrastructure.

text: Dedicated single-tenant infrastructure for training foundation models and serving inference at scale
quote: Train foundation models and serve billions of tokens on dedicated, single-tenant infrastructure.

text: Guides cover fine-tuning models and hosting load-balanced inference API servers
quote: Whether you're looking to fine-tune a model or host a load-balanced API server for inference, we have a guide for you.

text: Support is provided under customer service level agreements
quote: Lambda provides support according to the service level agreements (SLAs) in place with the customer.
